title: RUN
alt_text: A small brass-and-iron engine runs in a dark stone workshop, its black flywheel turning. Beside it sits an identical bronze copy that does not move, then a long table of copies, all still. A close-up of the original's turning hub. A grey-bearded man with deep brown skin, in a charcoal work shirt and leather apron, holds an unfinished iron flywheel casting beside the running engine; he looks at it, turns to the camera and smiles. The two engines return and the word RUN appears in white.

location.name: Terracotta Army
location.why: Thousands of molded figures, perfect in shape, none of them alive. A mold takes the shape, not the work.

youtube.title: 028 | RUN ⚙️ #philosophy #motivation
youtube.description:
Someone copied your work. Perfect copy. Dead engine.

They copied everything they could see. Every contour. Every detail.

A mold takes the shape. Not the work that keeps it turning.

Run your mind. Run your systems. Build the next one.

And let them copy.

—

linkedin.title: RUN · NDCH 028
linkedin.post:
Anyone can copy what they can see: the product, the layout, the pitch, the look of the thing.

What they can't copy is what keeps it running. The judgement behind the decisions, the systems that turn effort into results, and the habit of building the next version before anyone asks for it.

A copy is a finished object. The original is a process that keeps going. If someone copies your work, the answer is rarely to guard it harder. It is to keep building.
